narrative:
The model determined that you have a 53% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the amount you requested, and the purpose of the loan. Your checking account being in negative balance (<0 DM) was the single biggest reason for the rejection. Among approved applicants, only 12.6% have a negative balance, while 59% have no checking account at all. This status strongly pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk.

The loan amount of 5,371 DM also worked against you. Approved applicants request an average of about 3,020 DM, so your larger request increased the model's concern about repayment ability and further increased the probability of bad credit.

The purpose of the loan, furniture and equipment, was the only factor that helped your case. This purpose is relatively common among approved loans and slightly lowered the risk score. Unfortunately, its positive influence was not enough to overcome the negative effects of your account status and requested amount.

You should focus on building a positive checking account balance, reducing the size of any future loan requests, and reapplying once your account shows consistent positive activity. This would likely improve your chances substantially.
